parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the division has no bathroom ban and 2013 anti-discrimination and hate-crime enhancement protections, classifying it as refraining from targeting trans adults, but unavoidable federal exposures dominate. Entry officers are instructed to refuse and seek evidence on document/sex discrepancy and may consider permanent fraud ineligibility; federal facilities must follow birth-sex rules; national custody policies since 2026 remove hormones and impose short hair/conversion-type therapy, with immigration custody abuse reported. State protections do not cancel federal screening, facilities, or custody. Minors face additional entry, school-investigation, and proposed care restrictions, several enjoined but unresolved.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal policy bars X/non-matching passport markers, existing X valid to expiry; 2025 cable directs refusal and evidence requests on discrepancy/doubt, and consideration of permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Trans-athlete entry ban also documented.
entry_documents.protection: Division anti-discrimination law does not govern federal entry; no documented federal remedy exempting visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to refusal, investigation and fraud consideration before any state protection applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections model from 2026: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. for federal custody; division custody placement policy not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud/investigation can lead to detention where birth-sex/national custody practices apply, overriding state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; many units ban public facilities, 4 criminalise in some circumstances, one documented arrest held in men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division itself has no ban on bathroom/facility use by gender identity per equality map; 29+ units and capital district also no mapped ban, but federal buildings remain under national order.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State permission protects state/local facilities, does not displace federal facility rule or federal custody/ward placement.

care_services.exposure: National orders target minor gender-affirming care, school pronoun use, funding and insurance; DOJ subpoenaed hospitals for minor records. Several orders blocked/enjoined, status unresolved.
care_services.protection: Division bans conversion therapy on minors and disciplines professionals since 2018; insurance gender-identity discrimination prohibited since 2016.
care_services.interaction: Visiting adult care and prescribed medication at federal/national level uncertain; minor care exposure depends on current injunctions and state protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National framing defines sex as birth binary, removes gender-ideology materials, May 2026 strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; cash-reward guidance lists radical gender ideology among extremist viewpoints.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; division has gender-identity penalty enhancement since 2013 and 2013 anti-discrimination act.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing and screening coexist with state hate-crime/discrimination protections; federal actors are not shown bound by state remedies.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans athletes barred entry to compete; order directs investigation/prosecution over school social transition including names/pronouns; proposed rules would bar public insurance for under-18 care.
minors_guardians.protection: Division conversion-therapy ban for minors and child-welfare bar; several national orders enjoined, but no guarantee for travelling minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor may face entry, school-visit, or care-access scrutiny that adult companions cannot override with state law.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific incidents, enforcement figures, or violence rates documented. National bias data is general and dated in part; 2025 poll shows majority support for birth-sex document laws.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division 2013 penalty enhancement for bias-motivated violent crime; national hate-crime law exists, only 23 units cover gender identity in state bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street-level protection in division is legally documented but outcome/enforcement for visitors not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport-marker suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; 2023 panic-defence bill disposition unknown; X licence position only as of 2020; custody placement locally not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Low-Risk classification means largely refraining from targeting, not specialising in protection; no documented visitor remedy mechanism for federal exposures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation means operative exposure can change Federal remedy not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 universal facility/document exposure with inadequate remedy, but here division itself has no bathroom ban and state anti-discrimination law, so slightly above 0.35 despite federal entry and custody harms.

Higher than 0.55: that case has repeated local service hostility with some working readmissions, whereas this regime adds federal discrepancy refusal/fraud risk, federal facility exclusion and documented custody hormone removal/abuse without documented federal remedy.

Well below 0.75: that case has accepted documents, identity facilities and enforced court compensation with only a dead-letter statute; here federal birth-sex document/facility rules are operative and hostile state threat framing is documented.

parsed.synthesis: State layer is comparatively protective: no local bathroom ban, anti-discrimination and bias-enhancement law since 2013, conversion-therapy ban for minors. Combined operative regime is nevertheless constrained by federal gatekeeping: entry discrepancy can trigger refusal and possible lifetime fraud finding, federal facilities follow birth-sex rules, and federal custody can remove hormones and has documented abuse. Those are universal, unavoidable exposures the state cannot cancel. Severity is below imprisonment-for-presentation regimes, but above jurisdictions with accepted documents and working visitor remedies, placing it in elevated risk.
